newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Daewoo bets its future on US auto market.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Daewoo bets its future on US auto market.

text.p: South Korean automaker Daewoo Motor Co Ltd is pinning its future on re-entering the U.S. market and the launch of three new models there, chairman Kim Tae-gou said on Monday.
"We have bet on the U.S. market," Kim told reporters after a the opening of a new assembly plant in southwestern Kunsan. "We expect to sell 30,000 units in the U.S. market by the end of this year."
Kim said he could not imagine failure for the three new models.
"If the new models fail, there's no future," he said.
Daewoo agreed to stay out of the U.S. market through 1995 as part of an agreement ending its partnership with General Motors Corp in 1992.
During their 15-year partnership, Daewoo and GM were frequently at odds, but Daewoo Group founder Kim Woo-choong hinted on Monday that a fresh tie-up was likely.
"Talks are under way for a sort of cross-production deal with GM. We expect to see something by around June," he said. It was not clear from his remarks whether formal negotiations had begun.

Daewoo Motor plans to debut its three new models -- Lanos, Nubira and Leganza compact sedans -- on the U.S. market and would aggressively target college students and professors as its main customers, Kim Woo-choong said.
"Selling cars to students and professors...will help us leave a strong brand image for the future," he said. "I believe we have the competitiveness."
Daewoo Motor officials said the Lanos and Nubira models were South Korea's best sellers in March.
Daewoo Motor is South Korea's third-largest car maker and a unit of the Daewoo Group, which ranks fourth among South Korean conglomerates or "chaebol" in terms of assets.

The new complex, which cost more than $1.3 billion over the last four years, includes a car plant with a capacity of 300,000 units a year, a truck plant with capacity of 20,000 units per year an export pier with a shipping capacity of more than 200,000 vehicles a year.
Completion of the complex has raised Daewoo Motor's annual vehicle production capacity to 1.6 million units, including 600,000 units in overseas plants.
Daewoo Motor has said it will expand its overseas vehicle production capacity to 1.5 million a year by 2000, bringing its global production capacity to 2.5 million.
Sales in Europe are also due to begin later this year and the group expected annual sales to reach some 150,000, Kim Woo-choong said.
Daewoo plans to sell 885,000 vehicles this year, including 400,000 overseas, compared with last year's overall sales of 653,098 vehicles, including 352,916 abroad.
Daewoo Motor, which earned 23 billion won ($25.7 million) in net profits in 1996 on sales of 4.3 trillion won, has set its target at 70 billion won in profits this year on sales of 6.8 trillion won.
